Mission-based airfoil ranking Instant ML polar prediction First-pass flight sizing No install, no licences
About the Project

Early design, without repeated CFD

This project develops an integrated, machine learning based conceptual-design tool for small UAVs, combining CFD-derived airfoil data, an in-house Gaussian-Process surrogate for NACA 4-digit polars, and first-pass flight sizing. It reduces the need for repeated CFD runs during early design and makes mission-based airfoil selection accessible to non-specialists.

Everything runs in your browser. Open the page, choose a mission, and go from airfoil selection to a first-pass performance estimate in minutes.

Key Innovations

Built for non-specialists, transparent for engineers

Mission-driven ranking

Pick surveillance, mapping, cargo, racing, reconnaissance or custom, and airfoils are ranked with transparent, adjustable weights for efficiency, lift and stall safety.

In-house ML polar predictor

A Gaussian-Process model trained on 128 XFOIL airfoils predicts lift and drag polars for NACA 4-digit airfoils, at any Reynolds number from 200,000 to 600,000, instantly in your browser.

Airfoil to aircraft

The chosen polar feeds directly into wing geometry, Reynolds number, drag, power, battery current, endurance and range.

Atmosphere-aware

Density, viscosity and Reynolds number come from the ISA atmosphere at your design altitude.

Platform-aware defaults

Built-in factors for eight platform types and a VTOL energy budget, so you never need to guess values like Oswald efficiency.

Score = w1·Cl/Cd + w2·Clmax + w3·α

Fully transparent

Every score and result follows a published formula you can inspect.

Accessible to everyone

No subscriptions, licences, installation, solver setup or CFD expertise required.

Model Accuracy

Validated on airfoils the model never saw

Trained on 128 NACA 4-digit airfoils (632 XFOIL polars, Re 200,000 – 600,000) and tested by 5-fold cross-validation: every airfoil was predicted by a model that had never seen it.

Cl Max0%
Cd Min0%
Cl/Cd Max0%
Stall AoA0%
Opt AoA0%
Average0%

Accuracy = 100% − mean absolute percentage error between the ML-predicted and the true value, over airfoils held out from training (cross-validated across all 128 airfoils). Opt AoA is the hardest output because the lift-to-drag peak is flat (average error about 0.5°). Reference polars are XFOIL results, a computational prediction rather than wind-tunnel data; valid for NACA 4-digit airfoils (camber 0–8 %, thickness 6–21 %) at Reynolds numbers of 200,000 – 600,000.

Important note. This platform is designed for conceptual design and early-stage screening. It does not replace CFD or wind-tunnel testing. Final designs should be verified with high-fidelity analysis before construction.

Module D — NACA Wind Tunnel Simulator

Real-time 2D flow visualisation (Lattice-Boltzmann D2Q9) around the NACA sections of your Verified Library.

The tunnel runs at a low lattice Reynolds number, so its live Cl/Cd are for qualitative flow visualisation. Quantitative values come from the Verified Library CFD polars (Re ≈ 300,000) shown above.

Wind tunnel is idle

Choose a NACA airfoil and angle of attack, then press Load in tunnel to start the simulation.

Library values at Re 300k are shown here. The calculation uses the XFOIL polar at your real cruise Re (200k–600k, interpolated).

Modelling assumptions: propulsive η (prop × motor × ESC) is the platform-typical value shown in the platform bar and held constant. Usable SOC is the depth of discharge including any reserve. Drag = XFOIL profile drag at the trimmed Cl + estimated fuselage/tail/misc parasite drag + induced drag.

Structure + electronics — Payload — Battery —
Battery weight = pack energy (V × mAh) ÷ typical pack-level specific energy of the chosen chemistry (cells, wiring, BMS, casing included). Usable energy = V × mAh × SOC%. Values are typical — confirm with your pack datasheet. VTOL hover adds ~40% power overhead during transition.

VTOL Hover Budget

Hover Power — W
Hover Endurance — min
Energy Fraction — %

Hover power from momentum theory: P = W1.5 / (√(2ρA) · FM · 0.80 motor/ESC) + overhead. Disk area left empty = automatic (100 N/m² disk loading). The hover share is taken out of the battery before cruise endurance is computed; idle rotors add parasite drag in cruise.
